chapters.title: Attendance Policy
chapters.text:
At YASH, we are committed to fostering a supportive work environment that enables employees to balance their personal and professional lives. To this end, we provide a variety of flexible working arrangements, including part-time work, telecommuting, flexi-time, job-sharing, and variable work schedules. These arrangements are tailored to meet individual needs while ensuring that business objectives are achieved. Employees can manage and update their work schedules through Infogram (our HR portal), subject to managerial approval.
## Flexible Work Options:
## Part-Time Work:
Employees may choose to work reduced hours while maintaining their roles.
The minimum required weekly hours for part-time work is 20 hours.
Employees must coordinate with their managers to establish a consistent part-time schedule that meets both their personal and business needs.
All part-time schedules should be updated in Infogram for tracking and alignment.
## Telecommuting:
Employees can opt to work from home or a remote location, subject to the nature of their work and with prior managerial approval.
Telecommuting is allowed up to 3 days a week, depending on business requirements.
Employees are required to remain available during core hours (9:30 AM – 6:30 PM) unless otherwise agreed upon.
Any telecommuting arrangements should be clearly documented in Infogram and agreed upon with the manager.
## Flexi-Time:
Employees may adjust their start and finish times while completing the required weekly hours (45 hours).
A minimum of 5 working hours per day is required, but start and end times can be flexible (e.g., starting at 8:00 AM and ending at 5:00 PM or starting later in the day).
Flexi-time arrangements must be agreed upon with the employee's manager and updated in Infogram.
## Job-Sharing:
Two employees may share the responsibilities of one full-time position, splitting the workweek and duties.
Both employees must agree on a work schedule that covers the full responsibilities of the role and ensures business continuity.
Job-sharing agreements must be approved by the manager and updated in Infogram, ensuring clear communication and responsibility allocation.
- Standard working shift: At YASH, offices are normally open 24/7. However, Company observes following standard shifts. Shifts may vary as per business need.

chapters.title: Leave Policy
chapters.text:

This policy assumes leave accounting year as 1st January till 31st December of the calendar year. An employee can apply or cancel leave by applying on INFOGRAM.
- Declared holidays will be limited to 10 working days (Fixed National/Regional & option to choose optional holiday) applicable for a calendar year i.e. from 1st January to 31st December
- Employees working at other location’s development center in India apart from their base location or working at client site shall follow the respective location calendar or client calendar as applicable.
- Whenever there is any change/modification in Holiday calendar applicable to an employee, s/he is responsible to request for change on INFOGRAM to avoid discrepancy in attendance.

chapters.title: Transfer Policy
chapters.text:
Transfer with in YTPL is classified as Transfer and Deputation:
[table]
| Sr. No | Type of Transfer | Duration |
| 1 | Transfer | Permanent movement of an employee |
| 2 | Deputation | Temporary movement of employee from 16 days to six months. Extension subjected t |
- Transfer: is permanent movement of an employee from one BG or SSG / BU or SSU to another with or without base location change within YTPL.
- Deputation: is temporary movement of employees from base location or place of posting if different from base location, to any of the YASH locations or client location for duration from 16 days including weekends & holidays to maximum 6 months. This location movement does not include a change in BG or SSG / BU or SSU.
- Conversion of deputation to transfer: A deputed employee may be transferred to the new location i.e. their place of deputation may become their base location or permanent work location if demanded by business contingencies & looking at the longevity of the requirement. Employee will also be eligible for claiming the relocation expenses as per the provisions of Relocation policy.
## Modes of transfer:
- Order transfer: Transfer initiated by company due to business need
- Request transfer. Transfer initiated by employee on personal need. Here, company doesn’t facilitate any arrangements & employee has to manage by self.
- Transfer process Except “Away on Global Assignment”: Transfer process shall be initiate & approved by following stakeholders on INFOGRAM as IRM/RMG HRPPRMG BUH BUH
- Transfer process - “Away on Global Assignment”: Transfer process shall be initiate & approved by following stakeholders on INFOGRAM as IRM RMG BUH HRPP
## RELOCATION POLICY
This policy covers the following aspects:
- Movement of new Joiners to the offered base location/permanent work location.
- Movement of existing Employees to transferred YASH location within India.
## For new joiners
Relocation expenses for a new joiner will be applicable from the “Location of most recent employment” to “Offered Base Location”, within India. In case reporting location is different than base location, please refer to possible scenarios mentioned in the policy
[table]
| Particulars | Entitlements for New Joiners |
| Travel arrangements | Travel up-to one way for self & family. |
| Food & personal incidentals | Not Applicable (NA) in case an employee is joining at base location or permanent |
| Local conveyance | Place of boarding or landing as per mode of travel applicable. This expense will |
| Lodging/accommodation | 14 days bachelor’s guest house accommodation at base location or permanent work  |
| Transportation of personal goods | Applicable from E1 & above grade as per section 7.0 of relocation policy. |
## Recovery of relocation amount paid
Amount reimbursed against the relocation expenses including all entitlements will be fully recoverable in case an employee resigns or employment is terminated for any reason before completion of one year of service for new joiners.
## Taxation
As per Income Tax Act 1961; relocation expenses are taxable in the hands of the employee even if supporting documents are submitted while it is expended for joining the company. However, relocation expenses are exempted up to the eligibility, provided employee submits the supporting document in case of transfers.

Employee needs to initiate resignation on INFOGRAM & date on which the employee has initiated the separation request will be considered as DATE OF RESIGNATION. However, employee will also have an option of RESIGNATION WITHDRWAL in system.
Resignation process shall be initiated & approved by following stakeholders on INFOGRAM
EmployeeIRM BUH HRPPCentral Offboarding Team
## BUSINESS ETHICS & CODE OF CONDUCT
This section presents a generic framework of principles to be followed by employees with respect to their conduct. The Code of Conduct acts a perpetual reminder of organizations accountability to build productive interpersonal relations based on values like Integrity, Honesty, Transparency and Dignity. Employees are expected to follow the same. Non- adherence may lead to disciplinary action including and up to termination of employment. Few of the important code of conducts which are expected to be followed are briefed below. However, the expectations are not limited to the same
- Avoid any conduct that could damage or risk YASH’s reputation
- Act legally and honestly
- Put the Company’s interests ahead of personal or other interests
- Ensure compliance with policies & processes
- Ensure compliance on mandatory trainings scheduled by YASH.
- Instill trust in fellow employees by listening, following through and keeping their word
- Strive to continuously improve the current process/ work methodologies for higher efficiency, accuracy or overall impact
- Treat individuals fairly and equally.
- Avoid Conflict of Interest
- Maintain, spread and practice respectful conduct with peers, subordinates & seniors.
- Use Company owned equipment for official purposes only. Negligence or improper handling which leads to damage of company-owned property is unacceptable.
- Use internet for business purpose only. Avoid any personal use other than self-development on technology frontiers.
- Use conference halls, discussion/ meeting rooms & guest cabin for business purpose only.
- Maintain confidentiality of business “secrets” of YASH client’s information or any other confidential information.
- Smoking, consuming liquor, drugs etc. is strictly prohibited at the workplace.
- Use of office email for personal communication, enrollment into web-based subscriptions etc. should be strictly avoided.
- Employees are expected to keep their cell phones on silent mode or with low volume ringing tone. Employees are suggested to avoid attending personal calls during office hours; however, if they are necessary, employees should take them from out of office premise.
- Inviting & attending personal visitors at office premise during workdays is not appreciated.
## ANTI-COMPETITION POLICY
The purpose of this policy is to comply with the Anti-Competition law, this policy is specifically targeted at those employees who are or may become involved with anti-competition law during their professional duty on behalf of the company.
It is compulsory for all employees to read and understand the policy carefully and ensure to comply fully with anti-competition laws.
Anti-Competition law’s general objective is to ensure that markets operate efficiently by providing competitive prices, product choice, and innovation. Anti-Competition Law is generally based on below underlying principles:
- To prevent anti-competition practices and to promote a fair and healthy competition.
- To eliminate agreement & practices having adverse effect on competition that restrict free trading and competition between business entities, promote and sustain competition, and ensure freedom of trade in the markets of India.
- The prohibition of abuse of a dominant position or of substantial market power; and
- The assessment of acquisitions and joint ventures to prevent the creation of dominant positions or the reduction of competition
Non-compliance with applicable national Anti-Competition laws can have unfavorable consequences which is just not limited to financial impact but also have adverse effect on reputation and viability of the company and is more perceived as unethical behavior.
In all operations and all functions supporting those operations, no employee shall engage in any conduct in violation of the Anti-Competition or competition laws. It is the responsibility of each employee to recognize potential Anti-Competition or competition law concerns as they arise and to consult & report to the Legal Department of the company.

chapters.title: Diversity, Equity & Inclusion Policy (Dei)
chapters.text:
At YASH, we are committed to fostering a workplace culture that values diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) throughout our global operations. We believe that every individual brings unique perspectives and experiences that contribute to our collective success. Our DEI commitment is reflected in our policies and practices, which aim to create a fair and inclusive environment where all employees feel valued and respected, with equal opportunities to thrive. We embrace and encourage a culture where associates are provided with quality job opportunities without discrimination based on age, color, disability, ethnicity, family or marital status, gender identity or expression, language, national origin, physical and mental ability, political affiliation, race, religion, sexual orientation, and socio-economic status. YASH is dedicated to an open, transparent, and merit-based recruitment process. We actively prevent discriminatory hiring practices to ensure equal opportunities for all job candidates, whether they are internal or external. Our employee selection process prioritizes qualifications and competencies, fostering an inclusive environment where every candidate is considered based on their abilities and potential.
The Associate can also write to corphr.india@yash.com for registering their concerns regarding the deviation of this policy.
## WHISTLE BLOWER POLICY AT YASH
This policy aims to create a safe and accessible environment for employees and stakeholders to report any suspected violations of company policies, unethical conduct, or applicable laws, particularly concerning information security issues. We encourage individuals (whistleblowers) to come forward without fear of retaliation, ensuring that concerns are addressed promptly and confidentially.
Importance of Reporting : Reporting is crucial for early detection, proper investigation, remediation, and deterrence of violations of company policies or applicable laws. Whistleblowing serves as a critical tool for maintaining good governance and transparency within YASH.
## What to Report
Whistleblowers are encouraged to report any of the following concerns:
- Corruption and Bribery: Reports regarding unethical practices involving the offer, payment, or receipt of bribes or any fraudulent activities.
- Anti-Competitive Practices: Instances of collusion, price-fixing, or other actions that undermine fair competition.
- Information Security Concerns: Breaches of confidential information, unauthorized access, phishing attempts, or negligence in safeguarding sensitive data.
- Discrimination and Harassment: Any form of unlawful treatment or harassment based on race, gender, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic.
- Misuse of Company Assets: Reports related to theft, fraud, or unauthorized use of YASH’s resources.
- Environmental Violations: Non-compliance with environmental laws or activities that cause harm to the environment.
## Who to Report To?
Dedicated Reporting Channel: Whistleblowers can report concerns related to information security by writing directly to whistleblower@yash.com. This email is monitored by the Compliance Officer, responsible for the initial assessments of reports.
Escalation: In exceptional cases, a whistleblower may also write directly to the Chief Operating Officer (COO) for urgent matters by using the following email: coo@yash.com.
## Reporting Procedure
- Prepare Your Report:
- Clearly outline the details of the suspected violation, including:
- Nature of the Concern: What specific policies, unethical conduct, or laws are being violated?
- Date and Time: When did the incident occur?
- Location: Where did the incident take place?
- Individuals Involved: Names of those involved or any witnesses.
- Any Evidence: Documents, emails, or other materials that support the claim.
- Submit Your Report:
- Use the dedicated email address whistleblower@yash.com to submit your report. Ensure that your message is clear, concise, and includes all relevant information.
- If necessary, you can escalate your concern to the COO directly via coo@yash.com.
- Confirmation of Receipt:
- Upon receiving your report, the Compliance Officer will acknowledge receipt within 48 hours. This acknowledgment will confirm that your report is being reviewed.
## nvestigation Process
Initial Assessment: The Compliance Officer will conduct an initial assessment to determine the credibility and urgency of the report. If the report requires immediate action, appropriate interim measures will be implemented.
Formation of Investigation Team: An investigation team, including members from the Compliance Department and relevant stakeholders, will be established to ensure impartiality and thoroughness.

chapters.title: Training and Awareness:
chapters.text:
Mandatory training sessions for all employees, including management, are organized to promote awareness of grievance policies and educate on appropriate behavior and reporting procedures.
Workshops may be tailored based on the nature of grievances reported to foster a culture of respect and understanding.
## Policy Review and Improvement:
An annual review of grievance policies is conducted to incorporate employee feedback and outcomes from past grievances to continuously enhance the remediation process.
By implementing these specific procedures for all types of grievances, YASH ensures a structured, fair, and supportive approach to addressing employee concerns, reinforcing our commitment to maintaining a respectful and inclusive workplace for all.
## ALLOWANCES POLICY
YASH recognizes & reward the earnest efforts of its employee for working in specific conditions due to business requirements. Situations which lead to extension of regular working hours due to improper planning, lack of time management or completion of pending task will not be considered as a condition of eligibility under this guideline.
All allowances are subject to work done by an employee under specific scenarios/conditions due to business reasons only as defined, approved & granted by a YASH as per guidelines defined & available on YOU Portal.
Specific Shift Allowance: Certain employees may be assigned to different work schedules and/or shifts and/or days outside of normal office shifts/days in accordance with the needs of Business depending on Client’s project(s)/ assignment(s), nature of work, committed deliverables, role of employee etc. while working from YASH offices. Specific Shift Allowance is a type of allowance provided to an employee for extra hardship by working in a non-standard shift for which an employee is not hired for. Employee must complete 9 hours in the shift and full fill the criteria of cut-off as specified below:
## Eligibility is as defined below:
[table]
| S. No | Shift Name | Shift Regular Time | Cut-off | Allowance Amount |
| 1 | Early Morning | 4:30 A.M. to 1:30 P.M. | Must work early in morning before 7:00 a.m. | ₹ 350/- per day |
| 2 | Night | 6:30 P.M. to 3:30 A.M. | Must work beyond 12 midnight | ₹ 350/- per day |
## Overtime Compensation Policy YASH values the commitment and hard work of its employees and recognizes that, at times, business requirements may necessitate working hours beyond the standard contractual obligations. To ensure fair compensation for such efforts, YASH provides additional remuneration for hours worked in excess or outside of the hours specified in the employees’ employment contracts. Eligibility for Overtime Compensation
## Employees are eligible for overtime compensation if they work hours beyond their regular working schedule as defined in their employment contract. Overtime is applicable in scenarios where the business requires additional working hours due to urgent project deliverables, critical deadlines, or other operational needs. Overtime compensation does not apply to hours extended due to poor planning or task delays caused by the employee. Compensation Structure
## Overtime Pay: Employees who are required to work beyond their standard working hours will receive compensation at a rate of 1.5 times their regular hourly rate, as determined by YASH, in accordance with legal regulations and company policies. This applies to all additional hours worked outside the contractual hours, including weekends and public holidays, where applicable. Non-Standard Shift Allowance: In cases where employees are required to work non-standard shifts (night shifts, weekends, or public holidays) as part of specific business requirements, an additional shift allowance may be provided. This is separate from overtime pay and is intended to compensate for the extra hardship of working outside of standard office hours. Conditions for Overtime and Shift Allowances
## Pre-Approval: All overtime work and non-standard shifts must be pre-approved by the employee's manager and aligned with business needs. Minimum Hours: Employees must work beyond their regular shift duration to qualify for overtime. For shift allowances, employees must complete a full shift (minimum of 9 hours) as specified by company guidelines. Recording of Hours: Overtime and non-standard shift hours must be accurately recorded and submitted for approval via the company’s designated time-tracking system. Exclusions: Hours worked due to employee inefficiency, poor time management, or the need to complete delayed tasks will not be considered eligible for overtime or shift allowances. Guidelines and Procedures: All details regarding the calculation of overtime, eligibility criteria, and other conditions are available in the company guidelines, accessible through the YOU Portal. Employees are encouraged to review the guidelines regularly to stay informed of any updates to the policy.

chapters.title: Compensation
chapters.text:
Your compensation at YASH is a competitive exchange you receive in return for your job performance & positive conduct. The approaches we take in designing compensation for our employees is based on inducing high positive drive towards the work and recognize employees on the value they bring and deliver to the company and its business.
The world is a changing place and so is the compensation. We remain in study mode to explore newer practices and modes in which we can compensate the wonderful contributions our employees make towards the vision and objectives.
We constantly endeavor towards building the best total rewards culture.
## MEASURES TO MAINTAIN FAIR AND COMPETITIVE COMPENSATION
The company is committed to maintaining fair, competitive, and adequate wages for all employees across its various locations in different states. A consistent and transparent approach is followed to ensure equitable compensation and compliance with all applicable laws and regulations.
- Periodic wage reviews are conducted across all office locations to ensure alignment with company policy and state-specific statutory requirements.
- Compensation structures are benchmarked against national and regional industry standards to maintain competitiveness in every operating region.
- Local economic indicators such as inflation, cost of living, and market wage trends are regularly monitored to ensure adequacy of pay levels.
- Full compliance is maintained with all applicable minimum wage notifications and labor regulations issued by respective state governments.
- Internal pay equity is evaluated across different roles, levels, and geographies to uphold fairness and consistency.
- The compensation framework is reviewed and updated periodically to reflect changing market conditions and organizational priorities.
- Proactive measures are taken to revise or adjust wages when required, ensuring continued alignment with employee welfare, compliance, and business sustainability across all locations.
## Equal Pay for Equal Work
The company upholds the principle of Equal Pay for Equal Work across all its locations and job functions. Compensation decisions are made solely on the basis of role requirements, skills, experience, performance, and qualifications — without any discrimination based on gender, age, caste, religion, nationality, or any other personal characteristic protected by law.
To ensure adherence to this principle:
- Regular reviews are conducted to identify and address any unjustified pay disparities across comparable roles and levels.
- Job roles and responsibilities are clearly defined and evaluated using objective criteria to maintain internal equity.
- Compensation practices are periodically benchmarked to confirm alignment with the principle of fairness and equal opportunity.
- All managers and HR personnel involved in compensation decisions are trained to apply these standards consistently and transparently.
- Any concerns or grievances related to unequal pay are handled promptly and confidentially under the company’s grievance redressal process.
## CTC STRUCTURE
The CTC structure at YASH is designed in line with the provisions of Income Tax Act. The basic components of your CTC structure will be
- Basic Pay
- HRA
- Child Education Allowance
- Food Coupons
- Statutory Bonus (If applicable)
- Provident Fund (Employer’s contribution)
- Gratuity
In addition, there may be some components like Special Allowance; Incentive etc. which may appear based on the customized design of CTC for you.
You may additionally opt for Leave Travel Allowance (LTA) component based on your choice & as per your tax planning. LTA is annual component paid at the end of financial year.
For more details on salary & tax related aspects; please refer SALARY TAXATION, SALARY COMPONENT & PERMISSIBLE DEDUCTIONS available on YOU (YASH Intranet Portal) at YOU > Shared Services >> Payroll >>> Library.
## LEAVE TRAVEL ALLOWANCE
Leave Travel Allowance (LTA) is the most common element of compensation adopted by employers to remunerate employees due to the tax benefits attached to it. Section 10(5) of the Income-Tax Act, 1961, read with Rule 2B, provides for the exemption and outlines the conditions subject to which LTA is exempted.
LEAVE TRAVEL ALLOWANCE (LTA) GUIDELINE is available @ YOU > Shared Services >> Payroll >>> Library. If employee wants to make LTA component as part of his/her CTC structure, then he/she has to apply on Infogram > Benefit Module.

chapters.title: Provident Fund
chapters.text:
Employee’s Contribution: This contribution is part investments an employee can make under section 80C (Please refer below) of the Income Tax Act.
Employer’s Contribution: This component is a part of employee CTC. It is calculated @ 12% of Basic salary. This is not part of taxable income.
## NPS (NATIONAL PENSION CORPORATE SCHEME)
NPS is an optional component, and employee can make NPS component as part of his CTC through Infogram > Benefit Module.
NPS is an easily accessible, low cost, tax efficient, flexible and portable retirement savings account. Under the NPS, an individual contributes to their retirement account while their employer to can co-contribute towards the social security/welfare of the individual. NPS is designed on a defined contribution basis where in the subscriber contributes to their account.
Employee must have PRAN number (Pension Retirement Account Number) before making NPS Employer Contribution as part of his CTC. To register for PRAN eNPS - National Pension System - NSDL
For more details on NPS you can refer NPS Scheme Guidelines available at YOU > Shared Services >> Payroll >>> Library
## OLUNTARY PROVIDENT FUND (VPF)
Contribution to Voluntary Provident Fund is option contribution to Provident fund account of employee. If employee wants to contribute more amount in his/her provident fund then employee has to opt for VPF Benefit through Infogram > Benefit Module.

## PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENT PLAN
An event of Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) can be initiated during various stages of employee life cycle based on performance review (except during initial 3 months from joining) and identified gaps between actual and expected performance of any employee. This identification will be based on certain measured & objectively defined attributes.
PIP is an initiative to seek performance improvement when the regular processes of mentoring, counseling, on job mentoring, support, written feedback may not show improvements in performance of an employee. PIP will only be initiated for an employee who has potential of being utilized by business upon improving his/ her performance.
Some indicative instances that may be illustrated here to depict the necessary & sufficient need of PIP are as follows:
- When an employee may consistently fail in delivering quality in his/her assigned task (goals) in a timely manner.
1.2 If during an absorption, confirmation &/or half-yearly review, an employee rating is 0- 2, PIP would be mandatorily initiated for the employee without BUH approval. If employee rating is 2.5 BUH approval is required, in case there is no response till 10 days on confirmation, it is deemed as an approval of PIP.
- Performance Improvement Plan - performance evaluation process is executed on Infogram, the HRIS system of YASH and shall work in a structured manner with direct involvement of the concerned employee, his/her IRM.
- PIP will be of a defined term of 30 days from ‘Employee Input & Process Acceptance’ step. Acceptance of PIP process on Infogram will be considered as employee’s acknowledgement on understanding the PIP process and the associated outcomes.
Employees will be given certain specific goals at the beginning of the term. The employee will be expected to work towards the fulfillment of the goals in the defined term. To assist in meeting the objectives, IRM, SRM will suggest the training & guidance required. In addition to the offered assistance an employee may ask for any assistance, support or mentoring from their IRM/SRM. This assistance will be limited to external facilitation only.
- Post initiation of PIP it is responsibility of IRM to review the progress of employees on completion of 15 days to provide feedback about the progress and in case any improvements are required further and a formal assessment at the end of the 30 days.

chapters.title: Disciplinary Action Policy
chapters.text:
This policy outlines the procedure and guidelines for handling cases of breach of acceptable conduct/behavior as defined by applicable laws, Company’s (YASH Technologies Pvt. Ltd.) polices and Code of Conduct which applies to all employees of YASH Technologies Pvt. Ltd (YASH) including permanent and contractual employees.
Any misconduct would be categorized as minor, major or gross misconduct wherein company reserves the right to define the category of misconduct based on the instance. Misconduct at client site would be considered as misconduct with high severity & result to that appropriate disciplinary action would be taken by Senior Management & disciplinary committee.
- Types of Disciplinary Actions: Following list can be referred as misconduct categorization but is not limited to as defined:
[table]
| Type of Misconduct |
| Minor | Major | Gross |
| Late Coming or Early leaving or extended breaks without permission | Breach of Anti Competition law policy | Breach of any agreement signed by employee or implied on employee by any specifi |
| Misbehavior | Breach of Applicable laws as an employee | Breach of Code of conduct |
| Unauthorized Absenteeism | Breach of company policies | Breach of company information security Policy |
| Use of abusive language | Breach of Health & Safety standards | Misappropriation and/or fraud of company documents and/or funds |
| Business Attire/Dress Code Violation | Breach of terms and conditions as specified in offer/appointment or any other le | Sexual Harassment |
| Tailgating i.e. making entry or exit in groups. | Consumption of drugs/alcohol at work or an event of company where alcohol is not | Theft |
| Abusing any policy & processes. | Insubordination i.e. refusal to obey orders | Unauthorized access &/or sharing of confidential/sensitive information of YASH/C |
| An employee escorting the visitor / vendor / client through tailgating without r | Integrity | Corruption in any dealings related to business and its funds |
| Escorting the prospective client without any approvals and authorized escort. | Misrepresentation/Suppression of facts | Persistent or repeated instances of misconduct. |

It is to be noted that all the proceedings of handling disciplinary action would be strictly kept confidential. Any person (including witnesses) who breaches confidentiality shall be subjected to strict disciplinary action.
Regardless of the outcome of disciplinary proceedings, the employee under enquiry, any person providing information and any witness, will be protected from any form of retaliation. Any unwarranted pressures, retaliatory or any other type of unethical behavior would be dealt with strict measures including and up to termination and legal action.
In case of sexual harassment case, proceeding of the case will be as per Anti-Sexual Harassment Policy. On Dap letter, employee signature will not be required as an acceptance. However, if employee is not satisfied with the outcome can escalate the matter at wecare@yash.com
In case any breach or violation committed by an employee tantamount to a criminal offence or severe aberration of any policy of YASH, legal action would be initiated by Legal team accordingly.

chapters.title: Grievance Redressal
chapters.text:
YASH being an equal opportunity employer is committed to creating a healthy working environment that enables associates to work without fear of injustice, prejudice, bias and harassment. Grievances committee is made to expeditious settlement of genuine grievances of employees in nexus to employment with the Company.
## Grievance redressal committee
This committee is an independent body includes members at Location level and Central level that work towards
- Providing a fair platform to raise grievance against any person/process/group of people.
- Adjudging the genuineness of the grievance raised by conducting thorough investigation of facts & quick settlement.
- Where any grievance raised would constitute an offence under the Indian Penal Code of any other law, the committee may advise legal consultation to complainant.
- To prevent any act by a third-party offender that may lead to grievance for any employee while on official work for the Company.
## Grievance redressal process
- An employee can raise any grievance by writing at wecare@yash.com
- The Grievance Redressal Committee would hold a meeting with the Complainant and record her/his allegations or statements & based on that Committee shall immediately proceed with the Enquiry and communicate the same to the Complainant and Offender.
- The Committee shall call upon all witnesses mentioned by both the parties & shall provide every reasonable opportunity to the Complainant and to the person against whom complaint is made, for putting forward and defending their respective case.
- The Committee shall complete the “Enquiry” within one month from receipt of written grievance and communicate its findings and its recommendations for action to the Chairperson based on which an erring employee can be awarded appropriate punishment.
- The Head-HR will direct appropriate action in accordance with the recommendation proposed by the Committee and guidelines of Disciplinary Action Policy.
In case of any suggestions or queries; please e-mail at corphr.india@yash.com.
## GLOBAL HARASSMENT PREVENTION POLICY
At YASH, we are firmly committed to fostering a work environment free from harassment. Every member of our team understands that harassment is prohibited by law and violates YASH policy.
To effectively prohibit, prevent, and deter acts of sexual harassment in the workplace, we have established a comprehensive Harassment Prevention Policy. This policy includes specific measures that we actively implement to prevent and monitor harassment, separate from grievance mechanisms and remediation processes.
## Preventive Measures
Clear Communication of Policy: All employees receive a copy of the Harassment Prevention Policy upon hiring and during regular training sessions, ensuring everyone is aware of unacceptable behaviors and the consequences of such actions.
Regular Risk Assessments: YASH conducts periodic assessments to identify and evaluate potential harassment risks in the workplace. This proactive approach allows us to address vulnerabilities before they escalate.
Anonymous Reporting Channels: To encourage reporting of harassment incidents, we provide confidential and anonymous reporting options. This empowers employees to come forward without fear of retaliation.
Active Monitoring: YASH has implemented monitoring mechanisms to observe workplace interactions and identify any behaviors that may suggest harassment. We hold regular feedback sessions to discuss workplace culture and any emerging concerns.
Support Systems: We have established support networks, including peer support groups and access to counseling services, providing employees with the necessary resources and assistance when needed.
## Response and Redressal
YASH responds promptly and effectively to any reports of harassment. Investigations are conducted thoroughly and discreetly, with appropriate actions taken based on the findings, which may include corrective measures and disciplinary actions, up to and including termination of services.
Our Internal Committee (IC) actively oversees the implementation of this policy, focusing specifically on the prevention, prohibition, and redressal of harassment cases.
